title: From commit to running release
summary: Follow one change from path selection through CI, an exact-source artifact, infrastructure deployment and a service release. The key is to ask what each green check proves, and which identity it proves it for.
opening_answer: CI decides which evidence a change needs and records the tested source. CD accepts only a qualifying successful Main push, deploys that source with retained image evidence, checks it, and promotes service versions through a separate smoke and rollback path.

blocks.text: Build, deploy and release are separate steps here. **Build** turns checked-in source into an image and records which image was produced. **Deploy** updates the environment’s infrastructure and configuration. **Release** moves a service alias to a candidate image and smoke-tests that service. Keeping them apart shows where a failure happened and what can be retried.

The automated GitHub Actions CI workflow runs on pull requests, pushes to Main, manual dispatch and a weekly schedule. A path classifier selects checks from changed files: focused owner lanes give quicker feedback, while shared inputs, workflow changes, uncertainty or unclassified paths select Full verification. Full mode is the broad source-bound gate; selected lanes make a narrower claim.

spec.title: CI: decide and verify

steps.label: Changed paths
steps.detail: A complete diff against the intended base is the input to selection.

steps.label: Select tier
steps.detail: scripts/ci/policy.py selects the required lanes, or all lanes when selection is uncertain.

steps.label: Run checks
steps.detail: The selected jobs test behavior, integrations, browsers, coverage and image inputs.

steps.label: Keep receipts
steps.detail: CI retains its selection record and source-bound artifacts for later gates.

spec.caption: A green aggregate means every check selected for that tier passed. It does not mean every optional check ran.

blocks.text: CI records a run attempt, the tested source SHA, the selection and build receipts. CD admits only a successful push-to-Main CI run from this repository and validates that exact run, source and attempt. The local receipt for `514914a` and hosted Main CI run `39415935595` (attempt 1, runtime source `629119c`) are separate results.

blocks.title: Selected versus Full
blocks.text: A green Dev gate covers the checks selected for that change; the Full verification gate adds inherited acceptance, combined coverage and exact candidate evidence.

sections.title: The artifact is useful only with its identity

blocks.text: A tag can be reused, so it says little about which bytes were built or tested. The delivery path instead chains four separate identities, each checked by a different step.

spec.title: Four identities, four checks

steps.label: Source SHA
steps.detail: The selection receipt records the tested source SHA. A pull request head SHA and its tested merge SHA can differ; the receipt, not a branch name, says which was tested. Old runs without a receipt stay unknown.

steps.label: CI run + attempt
steps.detail: Repository + event + commit SHA + run ID + attempt. CD accepts only a successful push to this repository’s Main and downloads artifacts from that exact run.

steps.label: Image config / digest
steps.detail: build_and_verify.py records each image configuration ID and runs it as the intended user (and Lambda identity where relevant). Pushed images are referenced by immutable digest.

steps.label: Scan receipt
steps.detail: v1_scan.py binds the Trivy result to the exact image configuration and source SHA. The gate requires zero fixable HIGH/CRITICAL findings; unfixed rows are recorded.

spec.caption: Each arrow is a recorded association checked by a gate, not trust inferred from a matching tag or name.

blocks.text: Every CI run uploads a selection artifact with its run attempt. Other jobs retain coverage fragments, service image receipts and candidate scan evidence. Full verification requires the selected jobs and their artifacts; a missing fragment is an error, not an empty success.

Automatic release starts from a completed CI run. The gate checks workflow name, event, head repository, commit SHA and run attempt. A PR run, a fork whose branch is also called Main, or a manual run is not an automatic promotion input; a manual exact-candidate Full run is review evidence only.

blocks.title: Two identity checks
blocks.text: A matching source SHA proves which code was tested. A matching image configuration or digest proves which built bytes were checked. A reusable tag alone proves neither.

sections.title: Deployment and release have different rollback boundaries

spec.title: What one automatic CD run does

layers.label: 1 · Admit
layers.detail: cd_gate.py refuses PR, failed, foreign-repository or non-push runs and pins the source SHA and run attempt.

layers.label: 2 · Deploy stack
layers.sub: Change set from the accepted source
layers.detail: The CloudFormation stack is updated in place. Unchanged images are kept; the plan lists which owners’ images changed.

layers.label: 3 · Release changed owners
layers.detail: Each changed owner (Media, or Processing with its worker) is scanned, promoted and adopted into the stack, then smoke-tested. A failed release smoke restores the previous alias. An owner whose migrations changed is deferred to a manual release with attest_additive.

layers.label: 4 · Public smoke
layers.detail: After Deploy completes, a separate step runs the upload-to-playback smoke. Stack update, promotion and this smoke are reported as separate outcomes.

layers.label: Not rolled back
layers.detail: Restoring an alias restores service code only. Migrations must stay additive so the previous and candidate images both work with the current schema.

spec.caption: Runs are serialized because the environment journal and account capacity are shared. Manual dispatch adds read-only preflight and review-only modes.

blocks.text: The final delivery receipt binds these steps to Main CI `39415935595` and CD `39416747925`, both attempt 1, with source `629119c5b3bd390ce072df0a43fe926cd7a161c7`.

Database compatibility is the constraint that makes image rollback safer than schema rollback. A migration that drops or renames a field can make the previous application image unusable. The release path therefore expects additive migrations and records an explicit operator attestation that both the previous and candidate images work with the checkout’s schema head. A successful image rollback restores service code and aliases; it does not reverse database schema. Design migrations so old and new versions can coexist during deployment, then remove obsolete schema only in a later, separately reviewed change.

sections.title: Use real receipts to explain failure

blocks.text: The current Main record is the clearest end-to-end example. Full CI `39415935595` passed on exact source `629119c` (25 jobs succeeded; three intentional skips, including two unconfigured advisory Sonar jobs). CD `39416747925` admitted that exact run and attempt. Its Deploy step, including owner promotion and stack adoption, completed at 12:04:26 UTC. The following upload-to-playback smoke completed at 12:06:34 UTC: upload returned 204, the job reached `done`, the encoder exited 0, and MP4 plus HLS playlist/segment playback passed. Read-only AWS checks then matched all three deployed image manifests, ten Lambda aliases and the ECS worker definition. This is a point-in-time delivery receipt, not team acceptance of a replacement submission freeze.

Keep the workflow repairs in the chronology: attempt #281 failed at startup because a runner context was used while configuring a job; the context handling was corrected and actionlint passed across all five workflows. Attempt #282 caught changed bytes in an already released migration; the exact historical bytes were restored and the deployment compatibility guard stayed enabled. The successful full CI and CD above followed those fixes. This teaches why a gate should reject invalid runner context and migration-history mutation before delivery.

Deployment success is not the same as every objective passing. The V2-live queue-wait observation remains about 37 seconds against a 20-second target; the earlier V1 cap-2 scaling target was missed, and the 30-clip workload was not run. The documented rollback restored a bad Processing candidate from source `7928b7c`, an older source-bound experiment. It does not prove rollback of `629119c` or reverse a database migration. Keep these older experiments separate from the current delivery.

blocks.q: Why can a successful CI run still be rejected by CD?
blocks.a: The run may be for a pull request, another repository, or a non-push event. Automatic CD requires successful CI for a push to Main in the same repository and validates the exact run identity.

blocks.q: If release smoke fails, what does rollback restore?
blocks.a: The previous service image alias. The database schema is not reversed, so migrations must remain compatible with both application versions.

blocks.q: Does a green rollback job mean the candidate worked?
blocks.a: No. It can mean the candidate failed as expected and the system restored the known-good alias. The candidate smoke result and the restoration outcome are separate results.

blocks.q: Why not release by tag alone?
blocks.a: Tags can be reused. CD checks source and run identity, while image receipts bind the tested source to a particular image configuration or digest.

blocks.q: What is the key explanation when a deploy fails after infrastructure updates?
blocks.a: Name which stage passed, which later stage failed, the evidence identity, and whether the failure was product behavior, orchestration, or a deliberate gate. The V2-live receipts show these can differ.

takeaways: CI selection is based on changed paths; uncertainty selects broader verification.
A green tier proves its selected checks only. Full verification adds inherited acceptance, combined coverage and exact candidate evidence.
Every receipt is tied to repository, event, source SHA, run attempt and image identity.
Deployment changes infrastructure; release promotes a service image behind a smoke and restoration boundary.
Image rollback does not roll back database schema; use additive, compatible migrations.
